Disrumpo.notes_markdown:
### Added

- **MorphPad node positions shape the sound, and can be automated** — Dragging a node on the MorphPad used to move only its dot; the engine kept every node in its corner. A node's place is now a parameter pair per band and node (**B1 N1 Pos X**, **B1 N1 Pos Y** and so on), so dragging a node changes the blend in 2D Planar and 2D Radial, and a host can automate it. In 1D Linear the nodes sit on the line instead, each at its own **Line Pos** (A at the start, B at the end, C in the middle, D three quarters of the way), apart from its 2D place, so switching modes moves nothing; dragging a node there slides it along the line. Positions are saved with the project. Projects and presets saved before 1.1.0 load as they sounded: every node in its corner, and the even spacing on the line.
- **User manual and signal-flow diagram** — Disrumpo's page on krateaudio.com now links a full user manual and a diagram of the signal flow.

### Changed

- **The MorphPad follows the band's Morph Mode** — The pad always drew and weighed the nodes as 2D Planar, so in 1D Linear and 2D Radial its blend lines and readout showed weights the engine was not using. It now draws the mode the band is in. In 1D Linear the cursor moves along X only.

### Fixed

- **Clicking a MorphPad node did not select it for editing** — The click highlighted the node on the pad, but the type, drive, mix, tone, bias and shape controls kept editing the previously selected node. Clicking a node now selects it.
- **Automating the custom sweep curve did nothing** — The Curve Point Count and Curve P0 X to Curve P7 Y parameters reached the processor and were dropped, so the curve only changed when a project was loaded. They now reshape the curve while playing.
- **Sweep Falloff and LFO Retrigger showed the wrong default** — Sweep Falloff showed Hard and LFO 1 and LFO 2 Retrigger showed off, while a new instance runs Soft and on. A host's "reset to default" therefore changed the sound. They now default to Soft and on.

Gradus.notes_markdown:
### Added

- **Signal-flow diagram** — Gradus's page on krateaudio.com now links a diagram of the MIDI flow, from note input through the arpeggiator and MIDI Delay to the MIDI output and the audition voice.

### Fixed

- **Retrigger Beat restarted the pattern on every block** — Gradus never passed the host's playback position to the arpeggiator, so it found a bar line at the start of every audio block and restarted the pattern there. Retrigger Beat now restarts the pattern on the host's bar lines.
- **MIDI Delay echoed each note with the next step's delay settings** — The DELAY lane's step was read once per audio block, after the arpeggiator had already moved past the notes it played. Every note in the block was echoed with the next step's settings. Each echo now uses the delay step of the note it echoes.

Innexus.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A possible crash when a host shut Innexus down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone. The Sync switch on the two modulator panels also no longer touches freed memory when the panels are taken down without an open window (as in automated tests).
- **A possible crash when opening the preset browser after a host shut Innexus down with its window still open** — In the same situation, clicking Presets read the preset list through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **The modulators used far more CPU than they should** — With a modulator on, every voice recomputed the pan position of all its partials on every sample, even when no modulator targeted Pan, and evolution rebuilt about 8 KB of scratch data per sample. Two modulators took about 7 % of one CPU core; they now take under 1 %. The sound is identical.
- **Modulator 1 set to Pan did nothing while modulator 2 was on** — Whenever modulator 2 was switched on, whatever it targeted, it replaced the pan positions of every partial with its own, so modulator 1's pan movement was lost. The two modulators' pan movements now add up, as their amplitude and frequency modulations already combined. Patches that use modulator 1 on Pan with modulator 2 on (among the factory presets, Ethereal Soprano) now move in the stereo field as set.
- **Live sidechain analysis could go deaf after one broken sample** — A single NaN or infinite sample on the sidechain input stuck the analysis's DC filter, so live analysis heard nothing from then on until the plugin was reset. Such a sample is now treated as silence, and analysis carries on from the next block.

### Changed

- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**

Iterum.notes_markdown:
### Added

- **User manual and signal-flow diagram** — Iterum's page on krateaudio.com now links a full user manual, covering all ten delay modes with every control, and a diagram of the signal flow through each mode.

### Fixed

- **MultiTap's Feedback did not repeat the pattern** — The feedback loop ran with no delay in it, so Feedback only softened the taps slightly and the pattern played once. Feedback now repeats the whole pattern, one pattern length later each time (the Custom pattern's length, or the time of its last tap), each repeat at the Feedback level of the one before.
- **MultiTap's HP Cutoff did nothing, and LP Cutoff kept filtering at its maximum** — HP Cutoff was never connected to the feedback filter; it now thins the repeats. LP Cutoff, once turned down, kept filtering after it was turned back to its maximum; at its maximum it now leaves the repeats unfiltered.
- **Digital's feedback above 100 % grew without limit** — Nothing inside Pristine Digital's feedback loop held it back, so above 100 % the repeats grew louder inside the delay line on every pass and only the output limiter hid it. The loop now saturates above 100 %, so self-oscillation stays bounded. Below 100 % Digital stays clean.
- **Digital's limiter let one channel duck the other** — One limiter ran over the left channel and then the right, so a loud left channel turned the right channel down too. Each channel now has its own limiter.
- **Tape's two channels ran through one shared transport** — The left and right channels shared one set of wow and flutter oscillators, oversampler and roll-off filter, so the wow and flutter ran twice as fast as set and the right channel started from the left channel's filter state. Both channels now share one tape transport and keep their own filters, so identical input gives identical output.
- **Tape and MultiTap mixed only part of a very large block** — In host blocks longer than 4096 samples, Tape left everything after the first 4096 samples 100 % wet whatever the Mix. MultiTap read the wrong dry signal in blocks longer than 8192 samples. Every sample is now mixed correctly.
- **Changing Spectral's FFT Size did nothing until the plugin was reloaded** — The new size was stored and only applied the next time the host re-prepared the plugin. It now takes effect while playing, with a short crossfade.
- **Switching modes could sound wrong in hosts that process in place** — During the 50 ms crossfade between modes, a host that uses the same buffer for input and output fed the old mode the new mode's output instead of the input. Both modes now hear the input.
- **Tape's head Level and Reverse's Filter Cutoff showed the wrong default** — Each head's Level showed +3.9 dB and Reverse's Filter Cutoff showed 401 Hz, while the sound started at 0 dB and 4 kHz. A host's "reset to default" therefore changed the sound. Both now default to what the processor starts with: 0 dB and 4 kHz.

Profundum.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **Sample & Hold and Smooth Random morph cycles repeated too soon** — The random generator behind these two cycle shapes overflowed and cycled after about 79,000 values instead of running its full sequence. It now runs the full sequence, so these shapes play a different random pattern than before.
- **The stereo field's band split lost precision at low frequencies** — Its crossover filters now run in double precision, which removes a small level error at low split frequencies, largest at high sample rates.
- **A possible crash when a host shut Profundum down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **A possible crash when opening the preset browser after a host shut Profundum down with its window still open** — In the same situation, clicking Presets read the preset list through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.

- **Long preset descriptions were cut off in the preset browser** — The description under the preset list was a single line, so a long one ended mid-word at the edge. It now wraps onto up to three lines, ending with "…" if it is longer still, and hovering over it shows the whole text.

### Changed

- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**

Ruinae.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **LFO Sample & Hold and Smooth Random repeated too soon, and LFO 1 and 2 moved in lockstep** — The random generator overflowed and cycled after about 79,000 values instead of running its full sequence, and both LFOs started from the same seed, so two random LFOs at the same rate produced the same values. The generator now runs its full sequence and LFO 2 has its own seed. Patches using these waveforms play a different random pattern than before.
- **An LFO with Symmetry away from the centre could glitch at the end of its cycle** — In the last moment of a cycle the LFO could read one value past the end of its waveform table. It now stays inside the table.
- **Granular distortion could skip or double-process a grain** — When a grain ended, a neighbouring grain could be skipped or processed twice in that sample. Every grain now plays through in order.
- **The Tape Saturator distortion's Hysteresis model clipped hard, aliased and changed with the sample rate** — Its magnetic model overshot at every step and only a hard limit at the Saturation level held it, so it made a clipped, square-ish wave with audible aliasing, went silent or turned to noise at Saturation 1, sounded different at each sample rate, and its NR4 and NR8 solvers produced near-noise. It is now a stable tape model that sounds the same at every sample rate: a soft saturation with magnetic memory whose peak follows Saturation, with a softer, cleaner character. The two factory presets that use it were re-levelled to keep their loudness: Stutter Bass matches its old level, and Degauss Drift, raised to the top of its Master Gain range, is about 2 dB quieter than before.
- **Silence after loud material could cost extra CPU in some hosts** — Release tails and the effects' feedback tails fade through the tiny "denormal" number range, which the processor computes slowly unless the host has switched that off. Ruinae now switches it off itself while it processes, and restores the host's setting afterwards.
- **A possible crash when a host shut Ruinae down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **A possible crash when opening a preset browser after a host shut Ruinae down with its window still open** — In the same situation, clicking Presets (in the header or the arpeggiator section) read the preset list through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **The Transient modulation source missed most attacks and fired on held notes** *(shared DSP)* — The transient detector fired when the level jumped past a fixed point quickly, so it missed quiet attacks and most smooth ones, and at high Sensitivity fired on every cycle of a held low note. Without a sidechain it listened to Ruinae's own output, where a chord struck over the previous one's release barely raises the level, so it fired on the first chord of a phrase and almost never after. It now fires on every new note when no sidechain is connected, rising to the note's velocity (a legato note, which does not restart the envelopes, does not fire it). With a sidechain connected it listens to the sidechain and fires when its level rises against its own recent level, by 21 dB at Sensitivity 0, 12 dB at 50 % and 3 dB at 100 %, at any level above -60 dBFS. The 13 factory presets that route it now follow every new note; on a chord struck every 0.5 s their level changes by 0.3 dB at most.
- **The Spectral delay took 25 seconds or more to follow a change** *(shared DSP)* — The Spectral delay smooths every change over 50 ms, but its smoothing moved only once per analysis frame, so changing its Time, Feedback, Spread, Tilt, Diffusion or Width while playing glided for about 25 seconds at the default 1024-point FFT size and 50 seconds at 2048 (13 to 100 seconds across FFT sizes 512 to 4096), and with Sync on a tempo change drifted onto the new note length just as slowly. Every change now settles in 50 ms. The factory presets sound the same, because they load with these settings already in place.
- **The delay never switched away from Digital** — Choosing another delay type starts a short warm-up before the crossfade to it, and Ruinae restarted that warm-up every time it refreshed its settings, which it does on every audio block, so the switch never finished and every patch played through the Digital delay whatever its Delay Type said. Tape, PingPong, Granular and Spectral now play when chosen, including in the 82 factory presets that use them (31 Tape, 21 PingPong, 18 Granular, 12 Spectral). All three of the Tape delay's heads feed their echoes back, so in 23 of the Tape presets the echoes would have built up without end, or taken longer than 4 seconds to fade by 20 dB; their Feedback is lowered to the highest setting that dies away (for Dub Chamber, whose dotted-quarter echoes land after the notes stop, and Echo Bass, whose echo level pumps with an LFO, the highest that still fades steadily, by at least 6 dB over 4 seconds): Dub Chamber 0.80 to 0.21, Tape Shuffle 0.45 to 0.22, Chaos Machine 0.45 to 0.25, Echo Bass 0.42 to 0.28, Chaos Wind 0.42 to 0.29, Attractor Storm 0.40 to 0.25, Lorenz Choir 0.40 to 0.23, Comb Runner 0.38 to 0.28, Tape Groove 0.36 to 0.22, FM Grunge 0.35 to 0.23, Degauss Drift 0.35 to 0.25, Euclid Pluck 0.34 to 0.26, Dreamscape 0.32 to 0.28, Vowel Cloud 0.30 to 0.22, Warm Analog 0.30 to 0.23, Foldbeast 0.30 to 0.25, Sidechain Wash 0.30 to 0.25, Reese 0.30 to 0.26, Spectral Slide 0.30 to 0.27, Arp Tilt Cascade 0.28 to 0.20, Gate Strings 0.28 to 0.27, Tape Drive 0.28 to 0.27 and Velvet Strings 0.25 to 0.23. With a chord struck every 0.5 s over a held note, the level while the notes play changes by about 0.2 dB in a typical preset of each type (median: Tape 0.19 dB, PingPong 0.08 dB, Granular 0.19 dB, Spectral 0.23 dB). The four that moved by more than 1.5 dB were re-levelled with Master Gain to their previous loudness while the notes play: Echo Bass -2.8 dB, Chaos Machine -2.0 dB, Arp Tilt Cascade -1.8 dB and Vowel Ghost +1.6 dB. Arp Tilt Cascade still peaks at full scale, held by the soft limiter, as it did before. Particle Storm is 2.5 dB quieter and was left as it is, because its peaks already reach -0.05 dBFS and raising it would push them into the limiter.
- **Spectral Morph and Particle patches changed level with the host's buffer size** *(shared DSP)* — On a C minor chord struck every 0.5 s, Modulation Maze played 12 dB quieter in a host using 64-sample buffers than at 512 (-18.5 against -6.6 dBFS RMS) and 16 dB quieter at 32, and other factory presets were up to 34 dB quieter at 64 (Granular Fog). There were two causes. The Spectral Morph mixer played sound only in the buffers in which it completed an analysis frame (one buffer in eight at 64 samples, and one step in sixteen at every buffer size in Mono voice mode, which renders in 32-sample steps) and placed the next frame at the wrong point. The Particle oscillator started an extra particle at the start of every buffer, so the smaller the buffer, the denser the swarm. The Spectral Morph mixer now plays every sample, always 1024 samples (23 ms at 44.1 kHz) behind the oscillators (it was 512 at 512-sample buffers), and the swarm follows Density alone. Modulation Maze now plays at -7.2 dBFS at 64-sample buffers and -7.0 at 512. At 512-sample buffers, Arp Chaos Matrix, a Mono patch whose mixer had been near silent at every buffer size, came out 10.1 dB louder, Particle Cloud 4.0 dB quieter and Choppy Texture 2.3 dB quieter; their Master Gain restores their previous loudness. Particle Storm came out 5.9 dB quieter; matching its old level would put its peaks at full scale, so its Master Gain was raised only until its loudest peak reaches -1 dBFS, which leaves it 4.5 dB below its old level. Grain Scatter is 1.3 dB quieter, Particle Beam 0.7 dB, Granular Fog 0.6 dB and Modulation Maze, Ping Garden and Fission Cloud 0.4 dB, and every other factory preset is within 0.3 dB of its old level at 512-sample buffers.
- **Spectral distortion, noise, triangle, Sample & Hold and Pitch Follower patches changed level with the host's buffer size** *(shared DSP)* — On the same struck chord, Glitch Step played 5.1 dB quieter at 64-sample buffers than at 512 (-25.6 against -20.6 dBFS RMS), Half Time Crush 3.4 dB, Gut String 3.2 dB and Degauss Drift 2.6 dB, and 23 other factory presets differed by 0.5 to 1.8 dB. There were five causes. The Spectral distortion had the Spectral Morph mixer's fault: it played sound only in the buffers in which it completed an analysis frame (one buffer in four at 64 samples, one Mono step in eight) and placed the next frame at the wrong point. Ruinae refreshes every setting on every buffer, and choosing the noise colour the oscillator already had restarted its colouring filter, which drained the low end of pink, brown and blue noise, and choosing Triangle again restarted the triangle wave from zero, which made a low triangle up to 8 dB quieter at 64-sample buffers. The Sample & Hold's Slew and the Pitch Follower's tracking moved one sample's worth per buffer, so they ran 64 times slower than set at 64-sample buffers and 512 times slower at 512, and routes from them barely moved. The Spectral distortion now plays every sample, always 512 samples (12 ms at 44.1 kHz) behind its input, the noise and the triangle continue through a refresh, and Slew and tracking take the time they are set to at every buffer size. Glitch Step now plays at -20.4 dBFS at 64-sample buffers and -20.5 at 512, Half Time Crush -18.6 and -18.7, Gut String -22.6 and -23.0 and Degauss Drift -12.4 and -12.5. At 512-sample buffers, Tidal Lock came out 10.0 dB louder (its drone's resonator now follows the played pitch), Spectral Ghost 1.8 dB louder and Ping Garden 1.7 dB quieter; their Master Gain restores their previous loudness. Quantum Field's Sample & Hold now sweeps its spectral tilt fully, which drove it 7.6 dB harder into the output limiter; its Master Gain keeps the limiter's distortion where it was, which leaves it 3.5 dB quieter than before. Bitrot, a Mono patch whose spectral bitcrush played broken frames, came out 8.7 dB quieter and much cleaner: its bitcrush now runs at 4.75 bits instead of 6.25, which gives back the grit it had (-21 dB of distortion against the uncrushed sound, as before), and its Master Gain is at its 2.0 maximum, which leaves it 2.7 dB below its old level. Tidal Breath, a noise pad whose peaks already sat close to the quietest the bank allows, is 2 dB louder through its Master Gain. Particle Cloud is 1.1 dB louder, Rosin Halo 0.9 dB, Benjolin Drift 0.7 dB and Degauss Drift and Rusted Circuit 0.6 dB, Chaos Machine is 0.7 dB quieter, and every other factory preset is within 0.5 dB of its old level at 512-sample buffers (Formant Sea within 0.7 dB; its Spectral delay varies by 0.3 to 0.4 dB from one run to the next).
- **The Additive oscillator clipped above one partial** — It added its partials at full strength each and cut the sum off at a fixed ceiling, so any patch with more than a few partials played as a clipped, near-square wave: Arctic Frost's 128 bright partials spent 96 % of the time on the ceiling, the loudest pad in the bank at -2.3 dBFS RMS. The partials are now scaled so that their sum keeps the loudness of a single partial at any count and tilt and never reaches the ceiling, and they start at spread-out phases so their peaks do not line up; a one-partial patch sounds as before. The 25 factory presets that use it now sound as voiced instead of clipped, and their Master Gain sets them to the typical loudness of the other presets in their category on a struck chord, or as close as their peaks allow under -1 dBFS on a struck or a held chord: Arctic Frost now plays at -20.5 dBFS (it was -2.3), Solar Flare -17.6 (-0.7), Glass Shimmer -15.5 (-2.2), Dreamscape -14.4 (-3.9), Quantum Field -22.5 (-10.2), Fill Cascade -17.2 (-4.9), Euclidean Bells -15.8 (-5.7), Ratchet Bell -17.2 (-6.4), Arp Morph Sequence -15.7 (-5.0), Inharmonic Bells -13.8 (-5.3), Living Harmonics -13.8 (-6.1), Spectral Chop -15.8 (-7.7), Arp Tilt Cascade -15.1 (-8.4), Spectral Ghost -16.8 (-9.2), Metal Resonance -15.5 (-9.1), Aurora Bell -14.6 (-9.7), 3x5x7 Evolving -16.5 (-10.5), Additive Sub -12.6 (-10.3), Rosin Halo -15.5 (-12.7), Velocity Canvas -15.7 (-12.1), Dorian Cascade -15.9 (-13.2), Regal Fanfare -14.6 (-13.1), Vapor Arp -16.0 (-15.1) and Gate Strings -16.0 (-16.4). Digital Decay, whose 1.2-second attack barely opens on a struck chord, is set on a held chord instead: -15.7 dBFS there, its peak at -1 dBFS.
- **Modulation stepped once per audio buffer, so large buffers clicked** — The modulation matrix, and the per-voice routes, were worked out once per buffer and held for the whole of it, so a route moved in steps as long as the buffer: 46 ms at 2048 samples. A route to the morph, a filter, the tilt, the trance gate rate or the master volume then jumped at every buffer, which clicked on note-ons in Granular Fog at 2048-sample buffers (sample-to-sample jumps up to 0.80, against 0.16 at 64). Modulation now advances every 64 samples inside each buffer, on the same grid whatever the buffer size, so a 2048-sample buffer plays what 64-sample buffers play; Granular Fog now jumps by at most 0.16 at every buffer size. The Effect Mix destination and the arpeggiator destinations still update once per buffer (the delay mix glides between updates). CPU use is within 2.5 % of before (paired, pinned measurement on six presets: -1.1 % at 64-sample buffers, +1.5 % at 512, +2.3 % at 2048). At 512-sample buffers, Velocity Canvas came out 2.4 dB louder and Tidal Lock 2.0 dB quieter; their Master Gain restores their level. Self Osc Ping is 0.9 dB quieter, and every other factory preset is within 0.6 dB of its level at 512-sample buffers.
- **Notes started and stopped at the start of the audio buffer** — Every note-on and note-off, from the host and from the arpeggiator, took effect at the first sample of the buffer it arrived in, whatever its position inside it, so a note could start or stop up to 46 ms early at 2048-sample buffers (11.6 ms at 512) and arpeggiator steps landed on the buffer grid instead of their beat. Notes now start and stop at their own sample: Ruinae renders the buffer in segments split at each note, so a 2048-sample buffer plays what 64-sample buffers play. Pitch bend and per-note expression move with the notes, so an expression sent with a note-on still reaches it. The arpeggiator still picks up the notes you play at the start of the buffer, where it builds its pattern. CPU use is within 3 % of before (paired, pinned measurement on six presets: +0.9 % at 64-sample buffers, +2.7 % at 512, +2.0 % at 2048). On a C minor chord struck every 0.5 s, the factory presets whose level differed between 64- and 512-sample buffers by more than 0.5 dB went from 15 to 11, and between 2048 and 512 from 28 to 20; at 512-sample buffers every factory preset is within 0.9 dB of its previous level (Euclid Pluck 0.9 dB louder).

- **Arpeggiator and trance gate steps could land a sample late, depending on the buffer size** *(shared DSP)* — At the start of every buffer the arpeggiator and the trance gate line their step clock up with the host's beat position. They rounded the position within the step down, and the number, which is usually a whole sample, often came out a hair below it, so the clock started one sample behind and a step fired one sample late, at some buffer sizes and not others (a 1/8 step at 120 BPM missed at a fifth of the 64-sample buffers). It now rounds to the nearest sample, so every step lands on its beat whatever the buffer size. The bar position the arpeggiator's Retrigger: Beat mode reads had the same fault and is fixed the same way.

### Changed

- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**

- **Random, Sample & Hold and Rungler start the same way every time** — These modulation sources now restart their random sequence when the plugin is prepared or reset (playback start, a sample-rate or block-size change). Before, each restart continued the sequence where the last one left off, so the same project could sound slightly different depending on how often the host had prepared the plugin. Patches that modulate from these sources play a different (but now repeatable) random sequence: 16 of the factory presets, for example Arp Chaos Matrix, Fission Cloud, Particle Storm and Benjolin Drift.

Seraphis.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **The Aether reverb and the body's decay cloud ignored the fraction of their delay times** — Their diffusers' allpass interpolation worked out to a whole-sample delay. It is now a true fractional allpass. The reverb and decay textures change subtly: of the presets measured, Warm Static is about 0.5 dB louder, and Vast and Cathedral Moss moved by less than 0.1 dB.
- **A possible crash when a host shut Seraphis down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **A possible crash when loading a preset after a host shut Seraphis down with its window still open** — In the same situation, double-clicking a preset in an open preset browser loaded it through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **The FX delay took about 25 seconds to follow a change, and a synced delay started at the wrong time** *(shared DSP)* — The FX delay smooths every change over 50 ms, but its smoothing moved only once per analysis frame, so changing Delay Time, Spread, Feedback, Tilt, Diffusion or Width, a new tempo, or loading a preset glided for about 25 seconds. With Sync on, a preset or project started at a different delay time (250 ms, or the free Delay Time) and slid onto the synced note length. Every change now settles in 50 ms and a synced delay starts on its note length. Of the factory presets only Restless is affected: its first 30 seconds are up to 0.3 dB louder and slightly darker, and after that it sounds as before.
- **The FX delay's Width could make the channels cancel** *(shared DSP)* — The random per-frequency phase offsets behind Width drifted the same way on both channels, so at middle settings left and right came out nearly opposite and almost cancelled in mono. Width now spreads the channels apart without cancelling. Of the factory presets only Restless runs the delay with Width: it is narrower, and its master gain is raised by 1.1 dB to keep its loudness.
- **The reverb's feedback mix was not the same on every platform** *(shared DSP)* — The Aether reverb morphs between three mixing matrices, and part of that morph has no single natural path; which one it took was decided by tiny rounding differences in how each compiler builds the plug-in, so the Windows, macOS and Linux builds mixed their reverb lines differently (on Linux a dark Cavern setting let its low end die away about a quarter faster). The morph now follows one fixed path on every platform. The reverb texture changes subtly on all three; every factory preset stays within the loudness and stability checks the presets are held to.

### Changed

- **Stone Circle is brighter** — Its decay cloud is tilted 0.5 dB per octave brighter, so it no longer sounds almost the same as Deep Well.
- **Seed 15 plays a new variation** — With this release's DSP fixes, seeds 14 and 15 came out almost the same (their measured difference fell below what Seraphis guarantees between any two seeds on Linux). Seed 15 now starts from a different value, chosen to sit well apart from all the others on every platform. A project or preset set to Seed 15 plays a different, equally random realisation of the same sound; among the factory presets that is Tectonic, Ghost Choir and Vast. The other fifteen seeds are unchanged.
- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**

Vorago.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **The Cavern reverb and the body's decay cloud ignored the fraction of their delay times** — Their diffusers' allpass interpolation worked out to a whole-sample delay. It is now a true fractional allpass. The textures change subtly and some presets come out quieter; of the presets measured, Chamber Drone by 3.4 dB, Cathedral Void by 1.2 dB and Glass Sphere by 0.7 dB.
- **Ice Shelf, Slow Bloom and Spore Drift lost some of their character to that fix** — Each is built around one feature, and with the corrected diffusers it came through less clearly. One setting per preset brings it back. Ice Shelf and Slow Bloom: Cloud Spectral Gravity +0.10 → +0.50, which stretches the drone's partials, so Ice Shelf's icy body rings through again and Slow Bloom's budding partials stand out from the drone again. Spore Drift: Noise Wake 75 % → 50 %, so the granular dust stands apart from the rest of the drone again and its spores' backward-drifting ghost grains come through. Levels move by under 0.5 dB at each preset's loudest moment; over the whole note Ice Shelf is about 1.6 dB louder and Spore Drift about 0.5 dB louder.
- **Five more presets lost a defining feature to that fix, or ran slightly too hot** — Wind Through Basalt: Ghost Peak Level 15 % → 5 %, so the wind and hiss lead again instead of the ghost layer. Fogbound: Space Mix 90 % → 100 %, so the fog swallows the drone fully again. Steam Vent: Ecology Mix 70 % → 90 % and Loop Gain 54 % → 90 %, so its high-passed, whistling feedback loops are heard over the hiss. Teeming: Ecosystem Depth 15 % → 20 % and Event Rate 0.20 x → 0.14 x, so the colony is heard waking slowly and feeding on the drone. Stone Gravity: on one of the four seeds it is checked at, its loudest 10 seconds sat 0.06 dB above the −6 dBFS ceiling; its Master Gain is now −0.5 dB. Each preset's loudest moment moves by under 0.7 dB; Teeming's peaks rise by about 2 dB.
- **Choir of Absence ran slightly too hot on some seeds** — On one of the four seeds it is checked at, its loudest 10 seconds sat 0.4 dB above the −6 dBFS loudness ceiling the factory presets keep to. Its Master Gain is now −5.1 dB, which brings every seed below the ceiling with a small margin. The output limiter already held its peaks, so what you hear is a less squeezed sound: about 3 dB quieter on average and about 1 dB quieter at its loudest.
- **The reverb's feedback mix was not the same on every platform** *(shared DSP)* — The Cavern reverb morphs between three mixing matrices, and part of that morph has no single natural path; which one it took was decided by tiny rounding differences in how each compiler builds the plug-in, so the Windows, macOS and Linux builds mixed their reverb lines differently (on Linux a dark Cavern setting let its low end die away about a quarter faster). The morph now follows one fixed path on every platform. The reverb texture changes subtly on all three; every factory preset stays within the loudness and stability checks the presets are held to.
- **A possible crash when a host shut Vorago down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **A possible crash when opening the preset browser after a host shut Vorago down with its window still open** — In the same situation, clicking Presets read the preset list through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.

- **Long preset descriptions were cut off in the preset browser** — The description under the preset list was a single line, so a long one ended mid-word at the edge. It now wraps onto up to three lines, ending with "…" if it is longer still, and hovering over it shows the whole text.

### Changed

- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**
